newsitem.title: UK: Upside seen for British-Borneo shares.
newsitem.headline: Upside seen for British-Borneo shares.

text.p: Bullish sentiment is likely to surround British-Borneo even though the shares fell sharply on Wednesday following the announcement of a rights issue, analysts said.

Even sceptics, who felt the company was trading at a demanding premium to net asset value, believe the shares may pick up if only because rival brokers will probably double their efforts to promote the stock after their recent upbeat comments.
"The push is going to be upwards, which I don't really agree with, but I can see it happening after the flurry of positive notes," said one analyst, who declined to be named.
Meanwhile, shares in British-Borneo Petroleum Syndicate Plc, which have gained 72 percent shares so far this year, dropped 38-1/2 pence to 1,374 following news of a 167.3 million stg rights issue.
Besides the rights issue, British-Borneo also announced the acquisition of Conoco's interest in the King Kong gas field in the Gulf of Mexico.
That deal and the equity issue will lower the premium of British-Borneo shares over their net asset value to roughly 50 percent from 80 percent, analysts said.
Some argue this may be a reason to pick up the shares. "You're paying a lower premium over core asset, so arguably its does become a bit more attractive," said analyst Colin Smith at BZW.
The main reason, however, why Smith continues to rate British-Borneo a "buy" is because of the firm's exciting prospects in the Gulf of Mexico.
"The key thing shareholders are really interested in, is the return they are likely to make on that exploration programme: we think that is good," Smith said.
But other analysts continue to show reservation as no oil has actually been pumped up in commercial quantities. They still believe the premium is too high to chase the shares.
"The market is assuming too much success and not taking enough account of risks," one industry watcher said.
